about: Moon and Mars target sites. A value is null when it was not measured; null factors are left out of the score. Every value names its source (see the sources list at the end). 'value' is the reference value. For jezero, gale, southpole and apollo11 it is the value in the team's brief (used by the reference rankings in section 6); for the other targets it comes from the team's own sourced research. Where that value is not a measurement at the site itself, 'strict' holds what the site measurements alone support (null if nothing site-specific was found). Checked against the sources on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10.

meanTemp.note: Mean near-surface air temperature measured by MEDA over the first 250 sols (northern spring and summer), not a full Mars year.

swing.note: Daily air range, about -83 to -23 °C (JPL's first report: high -22 °C, low -83 °C).

coldGround.note: Air temperature (MEDA), not ground: NASA describes -83 °C as a typical pre-dawn air value, not the lowest ever measured. This is the brief's value; Strict data leaves it out because no ground minimum is given in our sources.

strict.note: The lowest ground temperature measured at Jezero is not given in our sources.

rain.note: No liquid rain: the air pressure is too low for liquid water to last.

albedo.note: From the team's source list (INTA record of MEDA albedo). That link could not be reached on 2026-10-09 to re-check the number.

strict.note: Albedo of the Jezero landing area from orbit, reported with MEDA results; rover readings near noon were 0.09-0.16.

targets.name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit (cave skylight)
targets.mission: Proposed cave shelter for a Moon base (seen by LRO; no landing yet)

meanTemp.note: Surface temperature of the mare plain around the pit, not inside it (the Moon has no air): mean of the LRO Diviner day-night curve, 218.5 K, in the 0.5° (about 15 km) map bin that contains the pit (all nadir data 2009-2015, 15-minute local-time bins; 43 empty bins filled by straight lines between neighbours). The 100 m pit is far smaller than the bin. The eight bins around it give 217.8-222.3 K. Inside the shaded cave a model gives about 17 °C (see facts).

swing.note: Highest minus lowest point of the same Diviner day-night curve: 394.8 K near noon minus 93.8 K just before sunrise. Each point is the average of all observations in one 15-minute local-time bin. A lunar day lasts about 29.5 Earth days.

coldGround.note: Coldest point of the Diviner day-night curve in the bin with the pit: 93.8 K at about 05:20 local time, just before sunrise. It is a bin average, so single readings can be a little colder.

albedo.note: Not used: the only site value found is LOLA's laser normal albedo at 1064 nm (0.156, zero phase angle), a different quantity from the broadband surface albedo of the Earth sites (see facts).
